source: NASA POWER climatology 2001-2020; Open-Meteo elevation; NASA GIBS/MODIS Terra true color (2020, multiple dates)

sites.name: Atacama Desert
sites.summary: The benchmark hyper-arid desert. Clear skies, salt basins and Mars-like soils, but heavily studied.

sites.name: Puna de Atacama
sites.summary: A high-altitude Andean salt-and-volcanic plateau. Less crowded than the Chilean Atacama and rich in evaporites.

sites.name: Danakil Depression
sites.summary: Below sea level, hot, salty and hydrothermally altered. A brutal multi-extreme analog for early Mars and volcanic Moon terrain.

sites.name: Harrat Khaybar
sites.summary: A vast basalt field with lava tubes and cinder cones. A strong, under-studied regolith and subsurface analog.

sites.name: Namib Desert
sites.summary: The world's oldest desert. Linear dunes, dust and aeolian processes make it a process analog for Mars.

sites.name: Bodélé Depression
sites.summary: One of Earth's largest dust sources. A direct process analog for Martian dust storms and atmospheric mineral loading.

sites.name: Makgadikgadi Pans
sites.summary: A vast, flat salt pan with precise horizons and evaporite chemistry. Good for landing-zone and sample-return analog work.

sites.name: Nullarbor Plain
sites.summary: A flat limestone karst with caves and solution features. A candidate for subsurface and habitation analog studies.

sites.name: Chyulu Hills
sites.summary: Long basaltic lava tubes in a tropical setting. A rare accessible subsurface analog for lunar lava-tube shelters.

sites.name: Undara Volcanic
sites.summary: A well-preserved lava-tube system. Useful for testing subsurface mobility, shielding and habitat concepts.

sites.name: Kerguelen Islands
sites.summary: Remote, cold, windy and volcanic. An isolation and operations analog with strong logistical constraints.

sites.name: Devon Island
sites.summary: Home of Haughton Crater and the Haughton-Mars Project. A classic Mars analog, useful as a calibration site.

macrostrat.lith: limestone, dolostone, shale, evaporites, chalk; carbonate reefs

sites.name: Svalbard
sites.summary: Cold, dry and accessible. A polar-desert analog for thermal extremes, ice and low-light operations.

sites.name: Río Tinto
sites.summary: An acidic, iron-rich river with extremophiles. A benchmark analog for Martian aqueous alteration and habitability.

macrostrat.lith: conglomerate, sandstone, slate and limestone. coal

sites.name: Lonar Crater
sites.summary: A young basaltic impact crater with a saline lake. A compact analog for crater lakes, basalt and landing terrain.

macrostrat.lith: flood basalt(s); mafic volcanic rocks; basalt

sites.name: Qaidam Basin
sites.summary: A high, cold, hyper-arid basin with yardangs, salts and strong winds. A less-studied Mars analog candidate.

sites.name: Gobi Desert
sites.summary: A vast cold desert with dust storms and low vegetation. A process analog for Martian aeolian activity.

sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
sites.summary: The driest, coldest non-polar desert on Earth. A benchmark for polar desert and subsurface ice studies.

sites.name: Icelandic Highlands
sites.summary: Basaltic lavas, glacial outwash and wind-driven ash. A well-studied volcanic analog for Moon and Mars terrain.

macrostrat.unit: Tuff-breccia, agglomerate, or pyroclastic breccia, Pleistocene

sites.name: Wadi Rum
sites.summary: A protected sandstone desert with towering massifs, sand valleys and Bedouin access. A strong aeolian and field-operations analog.

sites.name: Erg Chebbi
sites.summary: A compact erg of high star dunes on the Sahara's northern edge. Excellent for rover mobility and dust studies.

sites.name: Waw an Namus
sites.summary: A remote volcanic crater with basaltic tephra and salt deposits in the central Sahara. Under-studied and logistically hard.

sites.name: Ol Doinyo Lengai
sites.summary: The only active carbonatite volcano on Earth. A rare process analog for alkaline volcanism and rapid alteration.

macrostrat.unit: Main-cone volcaniclastic rocks and lava flows

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni
sites.summary: The world's largest salt flat: precise horizons, evaporite chemistry and seasonal flooding. A landing-zone and sample-return analog.

sites.name: Pinacate Volcanic Field
sites.summary: A UNESCO biosphere reserve of maars, cinder cones and lava tubes. Accessible basaltic terrain for rover and subsurface tests.

sites.name: Mojave Desert
sites.summary: A dry, accessible desert with playas, basalts and strong dust activity. A practical operations analog with good logistics.

macrostrat.lith: metasedimentary, chert, limestone, sandstone, shale, minor phyllite, minor quartzite

sites.name: Craters of the Moon
sites.summary: A young basaltic lava field with lava tubes and cinder cones. A strong, accessible regolith and subsurface analog.

sites.name: Kamchatka Volcanic Field
sites.summary: A remote volcanic peninsula with basaltic lavas, ash and glaciers. A high-energy process analog with severe logistics.

sites.name: Kawah Ijen
sites.summary: An acidic, sulfur-rich crater lake with hydrothermal alteration. A Mars aqueous-chemistry analog in a tropical setting.

sites.name: Pinnacles Desert
sites.summary: A field of limestone pillars and karst cavities in an arid setting. A subsurface and construction analog.

sites.name: White Desert
sites.summary: A chalk and evaporite desert with dramatic yardangs. A low-cost, accessible testbed for dust and soft-rock operations.

sites.name: Axel Heiberg Island
sites.summary: A high-Arctic polar desert with ice, dry valleys and impact-like terrain. A cold, isolated Moon/Mars analog.

sites.name: Kangerlussuaq
sites.summary: A dry, ice-marginal polar landscape with road access and an international airport. A practical cold-climate analog.

sites.name: Death Valley
sites.summary: The hottest place on Earth, with salt pans, alluvial fans and extreme thermal cycling. A benchmark thermal-stress analog.

sites.name: Meteor Crater
sites.summary: A young, well-preserved 1.2 km impact crater in northern Arizona. A compact analogue for crater morphology and ejecta.

sites.name: Wolfe Creek Crater
sites.summary: A 880 m meteorite crater in the remote Kimberley. A pristine impact analogue with severe logistics.

sites.name: Lanzarote
sites.summary: A volcanic island with extensive lava tubes and basaltic terrain. Accessible subsurface and regolith analogue.

sites.name: Hawaii Volcanoes
sites.summary: Active basaltic volcanism with lava tubes and fresh flows. A high-fidelity lunar regolith and subsurface analogue.

sites.name: Socotra
sites.summary: An isolated limestone and desert island with unusual endemism. A remote karst and arid-terrain analogue.

ml.target: domain match score (0-100) per mission profile
ml.method: Profile-specific models selected by cross-validated ranking performance: RBF-SVR for lunar base/expedition, ExtraTrees for Mars. 5-fold CV on 34 real sites; uncertainty from 24 bootstrap SVR fits or ExtraTrees tree variance.
ml.caveat: Surrogate model trained on expert-scored sites. It reproduces the transparent domain rubric and provides uncertainty; it is not a substitute for field validation.
